request.spec:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A plan can now name one of its sheet's descendants, and its claims are generated on that sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the new "parent plans" test and the three existing scenarios.

**How it works**
- **Storing the sheet:** migration `V119__plan_sheet.sql` adds an optional `target_sheet_id` column to `plan`, and `Plan` keeps the value.
- **Adding a plan:** when a sheet id is given, `PlanService.add` checks it against the sheet's descendants and refuses it if it isn't one, writing nothing. If it is accepted, `PLAN_ADDED` gets ` sheet=<id>` at the end; plans without a sheet keep the old line unchanged.
- **Generating:** `generate` looks for the person with the same name on the named sheet, ignoring case. The claims go through that sheet's own claim service, so its rules apply and the `CLAIM_ADDED` records go to its audit. If no one there has that name, the plan makes nothing and is skipped. Plan dates are still worked out from the plan's own sheet's today, and the plan's made count still goes up.
- **Front end:** the plan form has a new optional `plan-form-sheet` field. Each plan row shows the named sheet (new `plan-sheet` testid), and the API returns it as `sheet`.

**Choices to check**
- A plan whose person has no namesake on the named sheet doesn't mark its dates as done. If someone with that name is added there later, the next generate will make the earlier claims too.
- The match uses names only, not aliases, because the request says "the same name". Changing this to include aliases is a one-line change.
